clue.text: Harry is frightful beast without love

indicators.note: here 'without' carries its old sense of outside, so the beast's name wraps around the next piece

parts.note: a dragon is a fearsome mythical beast
love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone calls a terrifying creature lacking affection a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: DRAGON goes round O, giving DRAG-O-ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to harass persistently, and dragooning someone is coercing or bullying them, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Figures the employees will be on the woman's side

parts.note: D and I are Roman numerals, 500 and 1
staff are the workers of an organisation

explanation.surface: The workers' statistics will support the female manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures' suggests statistics, but it means the Roman numerals D and I. 'will be on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The distaff side of a family is the maternal line, named after the spinning staff associated with women.

clue.text: Legal or crooked, this is certainly lively

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Whether lawful or corrupt, it's certainly lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this is certainly' is a link phrase before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning brisk and quick in tempo.

clue.text: A bloomer from a bovine point of view

definitions.meaning: a flower, the daisy so called

definitions.text: from a bovine point of view
definitions.meaning: as seen by the eye of an ox

explanation.surface: A flower seen through the eyes of a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: The daisy-like flower named after a bovine's organ of sight, and literally a steer's gaze.

clue.text: No rocky situation before debts become widely known

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or outcrop
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: Before debts get around, there is no trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky peak on Dartmoor-type moorland in England; IOU stands for 'I owe you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous, especially for something bad: infamous and much talked about.

clue.text: Think to imitate

definitions.meaning: to copy, as a mirror image copies its original

explanation.surface: Advice to ponder before copying someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder something is to mull it over, and a mirror copies whatever stands before it.

clue.text: Got up in a bad temper-is enraged in fact

indicators.note: the letters sit in the fact as written, tucked inside the words that follow 'bad'

explanation.surface: Someone stood up in a rage, truly furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Having stood or climbed up, past participle of a verb for getting up.

clue.text: A secret society member frames one, which is not right

indicators.note: something not right is wrong or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lodge brother sets someone up, which is unfair.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the fraternal order known for its private rituals and lodges.

clue.text: Time could well be pressing

definitions.meaning: the period at the end of the day
making level or flat, as an iron does to cloth

explanation.surface: Time is running out urgently.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of day after sunset, and smoothing out with an iron flattens things.

clue.text: The touch-line

parts.note: read not as the edge of a rugby or football pitch but as a straight line that touches a curve at one point

explanation.surface: The edge of a sports field.
explanation.walkthrough: The touch-line is the sideline of a football or rugby pitch, the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry such a line meets a curve at exactly one point without crossing it.

clue.text: Striking entails disruption

indicators.note: disruption throws things into disorder, so the letters of the neighbouring word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something remarkable brings upheaval with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient features stand out prominently, just as striking ones are conspicuous.

clue.text: Live in a glow-it's the illicit drinking place!

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the shining glow word

parts.note: a sheen is a soft glow or lustre
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A rowdy invitation to bask in warm light at a backstreet bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A shebeen is an unlicensed Irish or Scottish pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An unlicensed bar selling liquor without a permit, chiefly in Ireland, Scotland and South Africa.

clue.text: Additional support for fish provided by 23 down

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line
the answer to 23 down, a word for pressing clothes, is a synonym of iron

explanation.surface: An angler's extra kit is supplied by the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 down is PRESS; to press clothes is to iron them.
explanation.definitionFit: This L-shaped metal bar is used as a bracing member, an extra strengthening piece in construction.

clue.text: State the most important point

parts.note: main means chief or principal
E for east is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone declares the central argument of a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb but is the noun: a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A New England state of the USA, so a member of the Union.

clue.text: Horses tread on such amphibians

definitions.meaning: the elastic pad on the underside of a hoof, which the horse walks on

explanation.surface: Horses trampling tiny pond creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: The frog is the horny pad in the sole of a horse's hoof, and tailless leaping amphibians share the name.

clue.text: A docker devotes break to the engineers

indicators.note: break suggests smashing the word apart, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps

explanation.surface: A dock worker gives his lunch hour to the army engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A labourer who loads and unloads ships at a port.

clue.text: Give short change in error

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters in the two words before it

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper shortchanges a customer by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short change' reads as one phrase; split it, 'change' rearranges GIVESHORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip made through failing to notice something is a mistake.

clue.text: Leaderless men scoff about a venture

indicators.note: without its leader, the word loses its first letter
about means round, so the eating word goes around the small word next to it

parts.note: to scoff is to eat greedily, to devour

explanation.surface: Men without a leader gobble food as they set out.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt or undertaking, an effort to achieve something.

clue.text: Gloomy because of 23 down indeed!

indicators.note: the word 'indeed' splits, the first part telling us to put one piece inside the second part

parts.note: deed taken as written, the second half of 'indeed'
the answer to 23 down, a word for reporters, is used as it is

explanation.surface: Someone is sad because they were pushed down, really!
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' is read as 'in deed': PRESS goes inside DEED. 'because of' is a link, and pressed down also hints at the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low in spirits, dejected and downcast.

clue.text: A drop of French perfume

parts.note: de is the French word for of
a scent is a perfume

explanation.surface: A dab of fine Parisian fragrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall or downward slope, a going down.

clue.text: Operation of business backing in 23 down

indicators.note: in tells us the reversed piece goes inside the answer to 23 down

parts.note: the answer to 23 down, a word for reporters, used as it is

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A business backing a press operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of actions or steps toward an end, a procedure.

clue.text: Low point for some men-a dire situation

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the run of words are used, a stretch picked from inside them

explanation.surface: A dire situation brings a low point for some men.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point in astronomy, directly below the observer, so figuratively the worst moment.

clue.text: A measure taken in less interesting craft

indicators.note: taken in means absorbed inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: drier means more dull, less interesting
ft is the abbreviation for foot, a measure of length

explanation.surface: A shot of spirits is drunk on a duller boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishing boat using drift nets, a vessel and thus a craft.

clue.text: The judge is about to release about a quarter

parts.note: re means concerning, about

indicators.note: the second about means round, so the release word encloses the quarter

parts.note: to free is to release
E for east is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A judge is about to let go of a quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: An umpire in sport, the official who adjudicates.

clue.text: Strut by the sea

definitions.meaning: the land along the edge of the ocean

explanation.surface: Someone walks proudly along the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop or brace supporting a structure, and the coastline land by the water.

clue.text: He goes to the court even with a quite petty dispute

parts.note: plain means level or flat, so even
a tiff is a minor quarrel

explanation.surface: A litigious person sues even over trivial quarrels.
explanation.definitionFit: The party who brings a lawsuit to law, opposite the defendant.

clue.text: Reporters cause harassment

definitions.meaning: to urge or harass someone insistently

explanation.surface: Journalists hound people.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists collectively, and to pressure or urge someone insistently.

clue.text: Sound distortion is the difficulty

indicators.note: distortion bends things out of shape, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Audio distortion is the problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A knotty problem or complication, from the Latin word for knot.

clue.text: Observes a metal container is an unlovely thing

parts.note: to eye something is to look at or observe it
ore is rock from which metal is extracted, so it contains metal

explanation.surface: Someone inspects an ugly metal tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metal container' suggests a tin, but ORE is rock that holds metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ugly and offensive to look at.

clue.text: The veteran sort led astray

indicators.note: led astray suggests the letters wandering out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old soldier misled by some type of person.
explanation.definitionFit: An elderly person, someone who has been around for many years.

clue.text: Assayers of British coinage in years gone by

definitions.meaning: people who analyse metal to determine its quality

definitions.text: British coinage in years gone by
definitions.meaning: the tester was a Tudor shilling, later slang for a sixpence

explanation.surface: Assayers of old British coins.
explanation.walkthrough: A tester was a Tudor coin; the name later meant a sixpence.
explanation.definitionFit: People who examine metals for quality, and the tester was an old English sixpence coin.

clue.text: Spare book

definitions.meaning: an extra kept back, a substitute
to arrange in advance, as a seat or table

explanation.surface: An extra volume on the shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare player is a substitute, and to book a table is to secure it ahead.
